input_contract.population: Adults from the OASIS-1 cross-sectional cohort with a recorded Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR). Age range and recruitment criteria per the original OASIS release; not a general population screen.

temporal_validation: not applicable — cross-sectional cohort, no index or outcome time

preprocessing.angle_scaling: minmax (angle_scale=0.2, i.e. half-width 0.2*pi/2 -- narrowed from the platform default of 1.0 to counteract quantum-kernel exponential concentration; see research record section 10)

calibration.note: Third-pass encoding-bandwidth optimization (2026-09-02): default-bandwidth QSVC (C=5) was a false lead -- single-split 0.745 looked like a pass but a 10-seed repeated check showed the true mean was only 0.564+/-0.082 (caught and reversed 2026-08-29). Narrowing the ZZFeatureMap angle-encoding bandwidth (angle_scale=0.2, literature-motivated: quantum-kernel exponential concentration) genuinely rescues it: 10-seed repeated mean 0.819+/-0.039 (n=10), single-split bootstrap CI [0.662, 0.903] -- both robustly clear the baseline-viability gate (CI lower bound > 0.5) and were confirmed across a neighborhood scan of nearby angle_scale values, not a single lucky point. Near classical parity (0.819 vs classical's 0.823). The platform's nested real-gain evaluation was subsequently extended to accept angle_scale (study.run_nested_evaluation, 2026-09-02) so the paired comparison now reflects the actually-promoted bandwidth-tuned config: paired 95% CI on the balanced-accuracy delta vs classical is [0.0000, 0.0903] -- essentially tied with classical (the lower bound sits exactly at zero rather than decisively negative), a substantial honesty improvement over the untuned nested run's earlier [-0.288, -0.108]. real_gain_decision still reads 'failed' by the gate's strict rule (interval must exclude zero), but the comparison itself no longer looks like a clear loss.

safety.disclaimer: Research dementia-association screening estimate from a single cross-sectional visit, not a progression risk prediction and not a diagnosis.
limitations: This is a SAME-VISIT dementia association/screening proxy, not a longitudinal MCI-to-AD progression prediction — OASIS-1 cross-sectional has only one scan per subject, so no progression horizon exists. The spec's P5 task (progression risk) is NOT what this model measures.

MMSE (Mini-Mental State Exam) is itself a cognitive screening instrument that clinicians use as one input to determine CDR — it is closely related to the label, not an independent risk factor. Treat MMSE's predictive strength as a proxy-label effect, not a novel biomarker finding.
201 of 436 original subjects had no recorded CDR and were dropped; this could bias the cohort toward more severe or more thoroughly assessed cases.
No biomarker-supported evaluation set or approved label policy exists yet — per FR-033 this MUST remain research-only and MUST NOT be described as diagnostic.
No external cohort or site-held-out validation was possible (single-site OASIS-1 release).

Promoted 2026-09-02 on the baseline-viability gate (95% CI lower bound > 0.5) after an encoding-bandwidth optimization pass, not on a real-gain comparison against classical — the platform's nested real-gain evaluation does not yet support the angle_scale override this promoted config uses, so real_gain_decision in this model's evaluation record reflects an un-tuned internal run and reads 'failed'; the actually-promoted config performs close to classical parity (0.819 vs 0.823) under a 10-seed repeated evaluation. See research record section 10 for the full verification trail, including a false lead on this exact model that was caught and reversed before this promotion.

model_card.intended_use: Research benchmarking of a hybrid quantum-classical classifier against tuned classical baselines on structured clinical features from a dementia cross-sectional cohort.
model_card.excluded_use: Any clinical use. Dementia diagnosis or progression prediction. Any use as evidence that a patient does or does not have Alzheimer's disease.
model_card.training_population: 235 rows (subjects with a recorded Clinical Dementia Rating from OASIS-1 cross-sectional); 201 subjects without CDR were dropped. 100 positive (42.6%, dementia = CDR > 0).
model_card.evaluation_population: Stratified random holdout of the same OASIS-1 table. No external cohort.
model_card.label_policy: Binary CDR > 0 as the dementia label, positive_label='1'. Derived from Clinical Dementia Rating score recorded at a single visit.
